mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses equity valuations by increasing discount rates applied to future cash flows, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%, or the Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20d returns falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 4.5%, S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC between UNRATE and 5d returns is not negative (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based consumer demand contraction that depresses corporate earnings expectations, causing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS decline, S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is not negative (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising for 3 consecutive months), a higher federal funds rate level predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns due to reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: In periods of FEDFUNDS rising > 0.25% for 3 consecutive months, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS in this regime is not negative (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) reflects robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate profit growth, generating positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average, S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC between PAYEMS and 5d returns is not positive (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) falling below 1.7 million units (1700.0 in thousands) signals a weakening housing market that reduces consumer wealth and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 1700.0, S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC between HOUST and 60d returns is not negative (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a dual shock of weak manufacturing output and restrictive monetary policy, triggering negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: When INDPRO declines and FEDFUNDS rises, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is not negative (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions (GDPC1 growth > 3.0% and UNRATE < 4.0%), a decline in retail sales (RSAFS) signals consumer spending exhaustion, causing negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions (GDPC1 growth > 3.0% and UNRATE < 4.0%), a decline in RSAFS is followed by positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for RSAFS in this regime is not negative (Rank IC < 0.03).
